tasks.title: Implement ngv2/grounding_confidence_gate.py: compute_confidence(finding, signals)
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/grounding_confidence_gate.py exists and exports compute_confidence(finding: dict, signals: list) -> str.
Returns exactly one of 'CONFIRMED' | 'HIGH' | 'MEDIUM' | 'LOW' based on the specified rules.
LOW is returned if ANY signal is a known-FP match (result == 'known_fp', or kind == 'fp_filter' with result == 'match') regardless of other matches (known-FP dominates).
CONFIRMED is returned if there is no known-FP match and ANY signal is a structural proof (kind in ('taint_flow', 'formal_path', 'live_poc') and result == 'proof').
HIGH is returned if there are >= 2 independent tool matches (>= 2 signals with result == 'match' from distinct 'tool' values) and no known-FP match.
MEDIUM is returned if there is exactly one tool match (one signal with result == 'match') and no contradicting known-FP.
Returns LOW by default when none of the rules match (e.g. empty signals, or signals with no matches/proofs/known-FPs).
Module is stdlib-only, deterministic, and performs no I/O, database, network, LLM, wall-clock, or subprocess calls.

spec.objective: Implement a pure, stdlib+ngv2-only, deterministic confidence gate classifier compute_confidence() that ports the legacy grounding.py confidence algorithm to classify findings based on tool signal lists.
functional_requirements: Expose compute_confidence(finding: dict, signals: list) -> str which is a pure, deterministic, and total function.
Returns 'LOW' if ANY signal is a known-FP match (defined as result == 'known_fp', or kind == 'fp_filter' with result == 'match').
Returns 'CONFIRMED' if there is no known-FP match and ANY signal is a structural proof (kind is 'taint_flow', 'formal_path', or 'live_poc' with result == 'proof').
Returns 'HIGH' if there is no known-FP match and there are >= 2 independent tool matches that agree (>= 2 signals with result == 'match' from distinct 'tool' values).
Returns 'MEDIUM' if there is no known-FP match and there is exactly one tool match (exactly one signal with result == 'match').
Returns 'LOW' by default if no other tier rules apply, including when the signal list is empty.
Ensure exception safety: handle malformed inputs, missing keys, or incorrect types in signals/finding gracefully without raising exceptions.
Ensure total determinism: identical inputs must always produce the identical output without invoking datetime, random, or any external system.
spec.interfaces: exposes compute_confidence(finding: dict, signals: list) -> str
edge_cases: Known-FP signal alongside proof signal or multiple matches still forces 'LOW'.
Agreement on 'match' from same tool does not qualify for HIGH; tools must be distinct.
Signals containing extra keys or missing expected keys are handled without throwing exceptions.
Distinct casing or whitespace in values is handled or compared precisely according to the spec.
non_goals: Do not implement real static analysis, runners, symbolic execution, taint engines, or live PoC runners.
Do not perform FSM state transition or routing of the calculated tier.
Do not perform any network, database, file system, LLM, or subprocess calls.
spec.implementation_notes:
The module must import only standard library modules. Follow the highest-tier-wins rule in the specified order: (1) check if any signal qualifies as known-FP -> return LOW; (2) check if any signal qualifies as structural proof -> return CONFIRMED; (3) count distinct tools that have a 'match' result. If count >= 2, return HIGH; (4) if count == 1, return MEDIUM; (5) default to LOW. Make sure to adhere to the credential-naming constraint (avoid variable names containing secret/password/key).

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Mock findings dicts, mock signal list fixtures covering all combinations of results (match, clean, proof, known_fp) and kinds (pattern, semgrep, fp_filter, taint_flow, formal_path, live_poc).

token_budget_ratio.note: Pure function with conditional logic; testing requires covering multiple tier priorities and combinations of inputs, hence test budget is larger.
